title: Danny and the Two Shovels
synopsis: Danny keeps using his shovel; Sam finds another way to play, and the friends build a small world side by side.

related_resources.reason: Emerging peer social skills and need for adult guidance. Not a directive to share any possession at any moment.
Examples of communicating wishes and considering context. No specific technique guarantees cooperation.
Explicit bodily safety and trusted-adult conversations; a toy-sharing story is not a replacement for this guidance. Safety is adults’ responsibility.

rationale_citations.story_anchor: He liked Sam. He wanted Sam to have fun. But he also wanted to dig the last three places in his garden.
rationale_citations.editorial_rationale: A kind boundary need not cancel empathy for a friend.
rationale_citations.evidence_scope: Guidance on turn-taking and expressing desires, not a test of sharing behavior.

rationale_citations.story_anchor: Sam had a river to make.
rationale_citations.editorial_rationale: Alternatives can preserve cooperation without forcing a toy transfer.
rationale_citations.evidence_scope: AAP encourages finding another toy or activity; the leaf-river solution is original.

rationale_citations.story_anchor: Danny brushed the dirt from the blue shovel and put it on the grass between them.
rationale_citations.editorial_rationale: The later turn is offered when the original activity ends.
rationale_citations.evidence_scope: Editorial choice about a possible peaceful negotiation; no universal requirement.

source_note: The manuscript is original fictional narrative. Citations apply only to stated parent-facing developmental rationales; they do not source plots or establish an effect from listening to this story.
